verdict.rationale: GitLab documents standard credential mechanisms (personal access tokens, OAuth 2.0, SSH keys) and programmatic access control ('Control user access programmatically to maintain consistent permissions'), which are the building blocks for issuing scoped credentials that an AI agent (e.g. GitLab Duo Agent) could use to call the REST API. However, the evidence pack never explicitly ties token/OAuth scoping to agent-specific least-privilege provisioning (e.g. no mention of scope lists, agent-specific token types, or per-agent permission boundaries). Missing for 10: explicit documentation of scope granularity/least-privilege options, agent-specific credential issuance workflow, and independent confirmation that agents actually use scoped rather than broad tokens.
